note: Uno+ rule-knob run: identical to uno1 except the game and the budget, which is sized in DECISIONS (~2.0M) rather than hands. Uno+ hands carry ~3.5x the searched decisions of plain Uno hands, so 50,000 hands here is uno1's 120,000.
_note_game: The one-variable experiment (docs/NEXT_GAMES.md par.2): same engine family, same net shape, same search, one rule set - draw always legal (atomic, cap 15), +2/+4 like-on-like stacking, the 7-swap with tracked knowledge, 9-card opening hand. Measured before training over 300 random games: forced turns 63.9% -> 18.6%, mean legal actions per decision turn 3.2 -> 3.8 (4.3 under greedy; the >5.0 target from the brief was missed - recorded honestly, the forced-turn collapse is the effect that matters). Trains on single hands, rated over matches to 500, same as uno1.
_note_stall: A hand always terminates against players who want to win, but an early near-random net banks cards: measured random-play hands run ~1,700 moves (p90 4,400). max_game_moves=2500 truncates the tail as a draw; the trainer logs how often.
_note_budget: 50,000 hands x ~40-59 searched decisions each is ~2.0M decisions, matching uno1 (120,000 x ~17) and run1-era Azul (24,576 x 52 = 1.28M). elo.jsonl now records cumulative decisions exactly, so the cross-game chart does not depend on this estimate.
